chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Amriki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the beggar who has a begging bowl in his hand: is his testimony accepted? He said, 'My father (peace be upon him) did not accept his testimony if he begged with a bowl in his hand.'

key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.فِي كَفِّهِ: In his hand (referring to holding a bowl)

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a beggar accepted in Islamic law if they carry a begging bowl?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that a beggar who carries a begging bowl (kaff) is considered a professional beggar, rendering their testimony (shahadah) unacceptable in legal contexts. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that habitual engagement in a specific trade or status can impact one's credibility as a witness, distinguishing between temporary need and established profession.
